document.title: Osama bin Laden: Taliban Spokesman Seeks New Proposal for Resolving bin Laden Problem
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), 1998 Missile Strikes on Bin Laden May Have Backfired
document.note: [Secret] Taliban spokesman Wakil Ahmed says the Taliban understand the U.S. wants bin Laden expelled, and that Kandahar is still seeking a way to resolve the issue. He says that had Kandahar been able to retaliate with similar strikes against Washington, it would have. He says a Saudi "pride" blocked an authentic proposal, and suggests the U.S. could kill bin Laden, though he asks that it not. Excised.

events.description: US Charge Eastham met Wakil Ahmed in Islamabad on bin Laden.
US cruise missile attack on Afghanistan; Wakil claimed 22 killed, 55 wounded.
East Africa embassy bombings attributed to bin Laden's network.
Taliban Supreme Court ruled insufficient evidence against bin Laden.
East Africa embassy bombings, which brought bin Laden's presence in Afghanistan to the forefront.
US cruise missile strikes on Afghanistan after the embassy bombings.
Taliban Supreme Court decision on bin Laden, which disappointed the US.
Charge Eastham met Taliban spokesman Wakil Ahmed to discuss bin Laden, Saudi ulema proposal and Pakistani pressure.
Bin Laden held an unauthorized news conference in Khost and made a statement after the airstrikes, violating the Taliban ban.
US temporarily closed its embassy in Bangkok and issued a threat warning for Vienna due to bin Laden threats.
Clinton scheduled to talk with Nawaz Sharif in Washington on Wednesday about bin Laden.
Wakil to return to Kandahar to meet a Pakistani delegation from MFA and ISI about bin Laden.
US Charge Eastham met Taliban's Wakil Ahmed in Islamabad; US demanded bin Laden's expulsion for trial, Wakil proposed joint Saudi-Taliban ulema process.
Wakil to return to Kandahar to meet a Pakistani delegation of MFA and ISI representatives about bin Laden.
US temporarily closed its embassy in Bangkok and issued a threat warning for Vienna due to intelligence on possible bin Laden threats (week before).
Charge Eastham, with POLCOUNS, met Taliban spokesman Wakil Ahmed for 90 minutes; Wakil sought a new US proposal on bin Laden and urged no more strikes.
US cruise missile attack on Afghanistan; Wakil claimed 22 Afghans killed and 55 wounded.
Bombings of US embassies in East Africa brought bin Laden's presence in Afghanistan to the forefront.
Taliban Supreme Court ruled insufficient evidence was submitted to convict bin Laden.
Cable Islamabad 008803 sent to State and repeated to Peshawar, Riyadh and Cairo.

relationships.detail: Taliban harbor bin Laden in Afghanistan.
relationships.quote: FOR HARBORING BIN LADEN

relationships.detail: Senior Taliban spokesman.
relationships.quote: SENIOR TALIBAN SPOKESMAN WAKIL AHMED

relationships.detail: Ninety-minute meeting at Taliban ambassador's residence.
relationships.quote: CHARGE (ACCOMPANIED BY POLCOUNS) MET WITH WAKIL AHMED

relationships.detail: Taliban had earlier talks with Saudi side on bin Laden.
relationships.quote: WHETHER THE TALIBAN HAD SPOKEN AGAIN TO PRINCE TURKI BIN FAISAL

relationships.detail: Pakistani delegation incl. MFA and ISI to meet Taliban in Kandahar.
relationships.quote: MEET WITH A PAKISTANI DELEGATION (WHO HE LATER SAID WOULD CONSIST OF REPRESENTATIVES FROM BOTH THE MFA AND IST)

relationships.detail: Taliban spokesman Wakil urged the US Charge to provide a proposal for resolving the bin Laden problem.
relationships.quote: HE ASKED CHARGE FOR A USEFUL PROPOSAL FROM THE U.S. THAT WOULD SERVE TO FINALLY RESOLVE THE PROBLEM.

relationships.detail: Wakil speaks on behalf of the Taliban and its authorities.
relationships.quote: WAKIL SAID THE TALIBAN HOPED THAT THE SUPREME COURT DECISION DID NOT CREATE AN EVEN BIGGER PROBLEM FOR AFGHANISTAN.

relationships.detail: The court is a Taliban institution whose decision on bin Laden is discussed.
relationships.quote: DECISION OF THE TALIBAN SUPREME COURT WHICH SEEMED TO CHANGE THE STATUS OF THE TALIBAN FROM HIS HOST TO HIS PROTECTOR

relationships.detail: Bin Laden was hosted by the Taliban in Afghanistan; the Supreme Court decision seemed to make them his protector.
relationships.quote: CHANGE THE STATUS OF THE TALIBAN FROM HIS HOST TO HIS PROTECTOR AND COLLABORATOR.

relationships.detail: Bin Laden's presence on Afghan soil became the forefront issue after the East Africa bombings.
relationships.quote: THE PRESENCE OF OSAMA BIN LADEN ON AFGHAN SOIL TO THE FOREFRONT.

relationships.detail: Wakil said the Taliban could not prevent the US from assassinating bin Laden in Afghanistan.
relationships.quote: SEEK TO ASSASSINATE BIN LADEN IN AFGHANISTAN, WHICH HE REPEATED HIS AUTHORITIES COULD NOT PREVENT.

relationships.detail: US meetings with Wali Khan and General Malik were cited by Taliban as suspicious; Charge denied conspiracy.
relationships.quote: WITH RESPECT TO MEETING WITH WALI KHAN AND GENERAL MALIK AND REPORTS OF U.S. "DELEGATION".

relationships.detail: US contacts with Wali Khan described as business as usual.
relationships.quote: MAINTAINING CONTACT WITH ALL THE AFGHANS AND WITH SIGNIFICANT PAKISTANI POLITICAL LEADERS.

relationships.detail: US contact with General Malik described as routine.
relationships.quote: MEETING WITH WALI KHAN AND GENERAL MALIK

relationships.detail: Reported US delegation visits to the Panshir Valley.
relationships.quote: REPORTS OF U.S. "DELEGATION". VISITS TO THE PANSHIR VALLEY

relationships.detail: Charge worked three years at the US Embassy in Nairobi and lost friends in the bombing.
relationships.quote: HE HAD PREVIOUSLY WORKED FOR THREE YEARS AT THE U.S. EMBASSY IN NAIROBI AND HAD LOST MANY AMERICAN AND KENYAN FRIENDS

relationships.detail: US viewed bin Laden as giving leadership and guidance to the East Africa bombers.
relationships.quote: BIN LADEN WAS THE PERSON WHO GAVE LEADERSHIP AND GUIDANCE TO THE PEOPLE WHO HAD DONE THIS.

relationships.detail: Charge warned Kandahar leadership of possible further US strikes.
relationships.quote: WE COULD NOT PROMISE THAT WE WOULD NOT STRIKE AFGHANISTAN AGAIN IF THE PROBLEM WAS NOT RESOLVED.

relationships.detail: Taliban leadership is based in Kandahar.
relationships.quote: THE LEADERSHIP IN KANDAHAR NEEDED TO DEAL WITH.

relationships.detail: Bin Laden held an unauthorized news conference in Khost.
relationships.quote: AN UNAUTHORIZED NEWS CONFERENCE IN KHOST

relationships.detail: Taliban imposed a prohibition on bin Laden speaking out and warned he would be prosecuted for sponsoring terrorism.
relationships.quote: TALIBAN-IMPOSED PROHIBITION ON HIS SPEAKING OUT.

relationships.detail: Charge asked whether the Taliban had spoken again to Prince Turki; Wakil said they had not.
relationships.quote: WHETHER THE TALIBAN HAD SPOKEN AGAIN TO PRINCE TURKI BIN FAISAL FOLLOWING THE INTERIOR MINISTER'S PUBLIC STATEMENT.

relationships.detail: Taliban proposed a joint meeting of Saudi and Afghan ulema to resolve the bin Laden issue.
relationships.quote: THE JOINT MEETING OF SAUDI AND AFGHAN ULEMAS COULD HAVE PRODUCED A SOLUTION

relationships.detail: Taliban gave the Saudis a proposal; Saudi pride blocked it.
relationships.quote: THE TALIBAN HAD GIVEN THE SAUDIS AN AUTHENTIC PROPOSAL FOR RESOLVING THE BIN LADEN ISSUE.

relationships.detail: Wakil had earlier asked Ambassador Milam what would happen if bin Laden were turned over.
relationships.quote: WAKIL SAID HE HAD EARLIER ASKED AMBASSADOR MILAM WHAT WOULD HAPPEN IF BIN LADEN WERE TURNED OVER

relationships.detail: Wakil said bin Laden's wealth had been seized by the Saudis.
relationships.quote: THE REST HAD BEEN SEIZED BY THE SAUDIS.

relationships.detail: None; omitted.
relationships.quote: THE TALIBAN WANTED A SOLUTION TO THE BIN LADEN PROBLEM.

relationships.detail: Clinton was to talk to Sharif about bin Laden in Washington on Wednesday.
relationships.quote: PRESIDENT CLINTON WOULD BE TALKING TO PAKISTANI PRIME MINISTER NAWAZ SHARIF ABOUT BIN LADEN ON WEDNESDAY IN WASHINGTON

relationships.detail: Wakil returning to Kandahar to meet a Pakistani delegation including MFA representatives.
relationships.quote: RETURNING TO KANDAHAR TODAY TO MEET WITH A PAKISTANI DELEGATION (WHO HE LATER SAID WOULD CONSIST OF REPRESENTATIVES FROM BOTH THE MFA AND IST).

relationships.detail: Pakistani delegation to Kandahar included ISI representatives.
relationships.quote: REPRESENTATIVES FROM BOTH THE MFA AND IST

relationships.detail: Charge represents the US government.
relationships.quote: CHARGE REITERATED THAT THE U.S. CONTINUED TO INSIST THAT BIN LADEN BE EXPELLED

relationships.detail: Wakil said the Saudis held the key and that a Saudi ulema delegation to Kandahar could resolve the bin Laden matter quickly.
relationships.quote: IF THE SAUDIS WERE PREPARED TO SEND AN ULEMA DELEGATION TO KANDAHAR THE BIN LADEN MATTER COULD BE RESOLVED IN “MINUTES, NOT HOURS."

relationships.detail: Taliban to discuss bin Laden with a Pakistani delegation including MFA representatives.
relationships.quote: MEET WITH A PAKISTANI DELEGATION (WHO HE LATER SAID WOULD CONSIST OF REPRESENTATIVES FROM BOTH THE MFA AND IST).

relationships.detail: Pakistani delegation to meet Taliban in Kandahar included ISI representatives (rendered 'IST').
relationships.quote: REPRESENTATIVES FROM BOTH THE MFA AND IST

relationships.detail: The Charge d'affaires discussed bin Laden's expulsion with Wakil in Islamabad.
relationships.quote: CHARGE REITERATED THAT THE U.S. CONTINUED TO INSIST THAT BIN LADEN BE EXPELLED

relationships.detail: Bin Laden is harbored by the Taliban, which pays a diplomatic, economic and military price.
relationships.quote: THE TALIBAN WERE PAYING, AND WOULD CONTINUE TO PAY, FOR HARBORING BIN LADEN

relationships.detail: Wakil claimed Saddam Hussein was the root cause of all these problems.
relationships.quote: SADDAM HUSSEIN WAS THE ROOT CAUSE OF ALL THESE PROBLEMS.

relationships.detail: US passed detailed material on bin Laden to the Taliban, who found it insufficient.
relationships.quote: THE MATERIAL WE HAD PASSED TO THE TALIBAN HAD FAILED TO PASS MUSTER

relationships.detail: Comment notes Wakil may be dealing with Mullah Omar's view on bin Laden.
relationships.quote: HE MAY BE TRYING TO DEAL WITH THE PROBLEM OF MULLAH OMAR'S VIEW.

relationships.detail: Recent Supreme Court decision on bin Laden; Taliban did not consider matter resolved.
relationships.quote: IN THE WAKE OF THE RECENT SUPREME COURT DECISION

relationships.detail: Taliban described as hosting bin Laden; the US feared the court ruling shifted them from host to protector and collaborator.
relationships.quote: SEEMED TO CHANGE THE STATUS OF THE TALIBAN FROM HIS HOST TO HIS PROTECTOR AND COLLABORATOR

relationships.detail: Bin Laden operates on Afghan soil under Taliban permission, accused of being permitted to operate.
relationships.quote: THE TALIBAN WERE ACCUSED OF PERMITTING TERRORISTS TO OPERATE ON THEIR SOIL. PREEMINENT AMONG THESE ALLEGED TERRORISTS WAS OSAMA BIN LADEN

relationships.detail: Pressure from the US, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and UN to expel bin Laden strains Taliban relations.
relationships.quote: HIS AUTHORITIES WERE NOW UNDER GREAT PRESSURE TO EXPEL BIN LADEN FROM FOUR DIFFERENT SOURCES--THE U.S., SAUDI ARABIA, PAKISTAN AND THE UN

relationships.detail: Wakil claimed bin Laden was once a trained guerrilla supported by the US; Charge denied US support or knowledge.
relationships.quote: BIN LADEN HAD ONCE BEEN A TRAINED GUERILLA SUPPORTED BY THE UNITED STATES

relationships.detail: Wakil alleged the US gave 'asylum' to General Malik.
relationships.quote: GIVING. "ASYLUM" TO GENERAL MALIK, WHO HAD BEEN RESPONSIBLE FOR THE DEATHS OF FIVE THOUSAND AFGHANS

relationships.detail: A US delegation reportedly visited the Panshir Valley.
relationships.quote: SENDING A U.S. DELEGATION INTO THE PANSHIR VALLEY

relationships.detail: Russian-proposed UNSC resolution would invalidate Taliban passports and block foreign relations; US opposed the draft.
relationships.quote: RUSSIAN-PROPOSED UNSC RESOLUTION, WHICH PROPOSED TO INVALIDATE TALIBAN-ISSUED PASSPORTS

relationships.detail: Taliban 'ambassador' resides in Islamabad.
relationships.quote: RESIDENCE OF THE TALIBAN AFGHAN "AMBASSADOR" IN ISLAMABAD

relationships.detail: Taliban were under heavy pressure from Iran at the time of the missile attack.
relationships.quote: THE TALIBAN WERE ALSO UNDER HEAVY PRESSURE FROM IRAN

relationships.detail: Eastham previously worked three years at the US Embassy in Nairobi.
relationships.quote: HE HAD PREVIOUSLY WORKED FOR THREE YEARS AT THE U.S. EMBASSY IN NAIROBI

key_claims: Wakil Ahmed said expelling bin Laden without religious cover or proof would cause the Taliban's fall.
Wakil argued Saudi Arabia held the key via a joint Taliban-Saudi ulema proposal.
US Charge insisted bin Laden be expelled to a place for trial and warned of further strikes.
Cable comment suggests disagreement within the Taliban, possibly related to Mullah Omar's view.
Wakil claimed the Taliban restricted bin Laden's activities hoping he would leave voluntarily.
Pakistani MFA and ISI representatives were to discuss bin Laden with the Taliban in Kandahar.
